<STRUCT_0001>
Let <MATH_0001> be a groupoid in algebraic spaces over <MATH_0002>.
Note that there are unique morphisms of algebraic spaces
<MATH_0003> and <MATH_0004> over <MATH_0005> such that for every scheme <MATH_0006>
over <MATH_0007> the induced map <MATH_0008> is the identity, and
<MATH_0009> is the inverse of the groupoid category.
The septuple <MATH_0010> satisfies commutative diagrams
corresponding to each of the axioms (1), (2)(a), (2)(b), (3)(a) and (3)(b) of
Groupoids, Section <REF_0001>.
Conversely given a septuple with this property the quintuple <MATH_0011>
is a groupoid in algebraic spaces over <MATH_0012>. Note that <MATH_0013> is an isomorphism,
and <MATH_0014> is a section of both <MATH_0015> and <MATH_0016>.
Moreover, given a groupoid in algebraic spaces over <MATH_0017> we denote
<MATH_0018>
which is compatible with our conventions in
Section <REF_0002>
above. We sometimes say ``let <MATH_0019> be a
groupoid in algebraic spaces over <MATH_0020>'' to stress the existence of identity and
inverse.
